issues.title: T1 vocabulary clashes with Distributions and SPSM exports
issues.scenario: The T1 example starts `using StochasticWeatherGenerators, Distributions`, then uses `Continuous(Normal; …)`. Distributions exports `Continuous` (Distributions.jl src line 46, a ValueSupport type). Core exports its own `curve(g, var, par; …)`, while SPSM exports TVP's `curve`. The T2 door (`swg[:TX].models[1]`, then `curve(m, :μ)` after `using SmoothPeriodicStatsModels`) loads both. In the 4.2 lane, SPSM 4.x exports `AR1` (the evaluated twin), and Blocks defines `AR1()`.
issues.what_breaks: Julia warns that both modules export the name and that uses must be qualified, then throws UndefVarError for Continuous in every T1 session. The same happens for `curve` as soon as an expert loads SPSM next to SWG, which is exactly the T1→T2 path. Blocks, which itself uses Distributions and must distinguish Continuous from Discrete ValueSupport, has to qualify the name everywhere. The student 'small consistent vocabulary' breaks at its first use.
issues.fix:
1. Rename the block, e.g. `Marginal(Normal; …)` or `ContinuousVariable`.
2. Make `curve` a single function: Core does not export its own `curve`; Blocks adds `SmoothPeriodicStatsModels.curve(::FittedGenerator, …)` methods, and the umbrella re-exports SPSM's `curve`.
3. Add a CI test that runs `using StochasticWeatherGenerators, Distributions, SmoothPeriodicStatsModels, DataFrames, StatsBase` and asserts every T0/T1 name resolves unqualified.
4. Document that the T2 door needs `] add SmoothPeriodicStatsModels`: it is an indirect dependency and cannot be `using`'d otherwise.

issues.title: Persistence by repr(spec) + eval is fragile, unsafe and missing class hooks
issues.scenario: load_generator 'rebuilds the spec by evaluating that text'. Core has no dependency on Blocks, RegimeHMM or Distributions, so the text `RegimeHMM(RR = Rain(amount = Mixture(Exponential, 2)…))` has to be evaluated in some module that has these names. Specs can hold data: Regimes(paper), Regimes(path = table), Regimes(data = eca37), and show prints `Regimes(pretrained(:…))`. Custom blocks (the RegimeAnalog θ holds a Dict{Tuple{Int,Int},…}) and T2b classes (KNN params hold a WeatherData) have no serialisation hook: the 'what a class implements' list omits one. The pretrained JSON stores flat SPSM coefficient vectors, and 5.1 plans a SoftmaxLink rewrite of the transition coefficients.
issues.what_breaks: (1) Loading fails for users of a lib alone and for any custom block. (2) A shared .swg.json runs arbitrary code. (3) Any cosmetic change to `show` breaks old files, the pretrained artifacts included. (4) Specs holding data do not round-trip as text, so the claim that 'show prints valid Julia' fails for frozen regimes. (5) A coefficient-layout change in an SPSM minor silently misreads stored vectors, a silent numerical change in a pretrained generator.
issues.fix:
1. Serialise the spec as a structured JSON tree: type tag, version and kwargs.
2. Add public `to_plain`/`from_plain` hooks per block and per class, with an erroring fallback, so `save_generator` names the type that lacks support.
3. Never call eval.
4. Version the format and keep a reader for every past version.
5. Store evaluated curves (A(t), p(t), μ/ρ/σ(t)) next to the coefficients, and on load check that the rebuilt model reproduces them.
6. Freeze the format at P8, not P0. P0 should dump neutral raw arrays only.

issues.title: SPSM 4.2∩5.0 is not a consistent common API, and 'third positional is always weights' silently reinterprets v4 calls
issues.scenario: (a) In v4, `fit_mle(SmoothAR1(d, T), y, z::Vector{Int}; n2t)` (fit/ar1.jl:66) infers K = maximum(z) when the model was built without K (fit/ar1.jl:129-133, documented at :60). Under 5.0's 'N-vector = weights', the same call is a K = 1 fit weighted by the labels 1..K. (b) The 4.x method `fit_mle(::SmoothARPeriodicHMM, Y, Y_past::AbstractArray{<:Bool})` (fit/smooth_hmm.jl:227) captures a Bool N×K weight matrix, and also captures OneHot if OneHot <: AbstractMatrix{Bool} and no more specific method exists. (c) `rand(hmm, n2t)` returns `y` in 4.x (HHMM_Bernoulli/periodichmm.jl:98-107, seq = false) but `(; z, Y)` in 5.0. (d) `fit(SeasonalFit, m::_SmoothHMM, Y, Y_past)` (smooth_hmm.jl:573) takes Y_past as a required positional argument.
issues.what_breaks: (a) is a silent wrong model with no error. (b)–(d) mean the premise 'the libraries use only API present in both 4.2 and 5.0: … keyword rand, fit(SeasonalFit, …)' does not hold method by method, so the pre-registered libs (compat "4.2") may break when widened to 5.
issues.fix:
1. Require typed weights in 5.0: `OneHot(z, K)`, a `StateWeights(W)` wrapper, or StatsBase `AbstractWeights`.
2. Make `fit_mle(m, y, ::AbstractVector{<:Integer})` throw "did you mean OneHot(z, K)? For integer frequency weights pass float.(w)".
3. Publish an explicit per-method table of what exists in 4.2 and in 5.0, and add a Blocks CI lane against 4.2.
4. Have the libs call only `fit(SeasonalFit, …; past)` (added in 4.2) and their own regime samplers, never SPSM's HMM `rand`.
5. Optionally, 4.2 emits `Base.depwarn` on the old positional forms. Pkg.test enables depwarns, so downstream suites see them before 5.0. This is not a shim in 5.0.

issues.title: Registration facts and timing: version skip, unregistered v3 pin, sequential 3-day waits
issues.scenario: General's Versions.toml for SWG contains only 1.3.1, and the local repo has only the tag v1.3.1. P0 pins fixtures to 'SWG 3.0.0 + SPSM 4.1.0' in a committed Manifest. P8 pre-registers Core → Blocks → classes 'at least 2 weeks' before release. The umbrella goes from 1.3.1 to 4.0.0. The local remote is `StochasticWeatherGenerator.jl` (singular), while General records `StochasticWeatherGenerators.jl.git`. The dev_pkg LocalRegistry (docs/add_local_registry.jl) carries the same UUID at 1.x-DEV.
issues.what_breaks: SWG 3.0.0 cannot be resolved from any registry, so the fixture Manifest must pin by repo-url plus git-tree-sha1. If test/reference is a workspace member, its dependency on SWG (UUID 3eadb0b9) collides with the root package's own UUID. Umbrella 4.0.0 fails AutoMerge's sequential-version check and needs `[merge approved]`. AutoMerge's install check needs a package's dependencies already merged, and new packages wait 3 days, so P8 takes at least 9–12 days with no slack (more if WGEN must follow RegimeHMM). Any slip runs into release day.
issues.fix:
1. Decide now whether to register 3.0.0, which makes 4.0.0 sequential and gives the fixtures a registry pin, or to skip it and plan the `[merge approved]` step.
2. Pin the v3 fixtures by git tree and keep test/reference out of [workspace].
3. Start P8 at least 4 weeks before release, or ask the General maintainers to batch-merge the monorepo packages.
4. Fix the remote URL.
5. Retire add_local_registry.jl and the dev_pkg entries.

issues.title: Launching Core and Blocks at 1.0.0 freezes struct fields and helpers that are not public
issues.scenario: The design's own examples access fields: g.params, g.spec.k, swg.info.selection, swg[:TX].models[1], ctx.y, ctx.name, ctx.n2t, ctx.period, ctx.z, out.values, out.innovations, and data.calendar (although WeatherData fields are 'private'). The T2b KNN class calls SWGCore.standardized_features, initial_day, circdist and copy_day!, none of which is in Core's export or public list. The precedent: OrdinaryDiffEqTsit5 and the OrdinaryDiffEq root both require `OrdinaryDiffEqCore = "4.15.1"`, so Core has gone through several majors.
issues.what_breaks: The first needed change to FitContext, SimContext, BlockOutput or FittedGenerator layout is Blocks or Core 2.0. That cascades into compat bumps in every class lib and, through re-exports, an umbrella major. Third-party class authors following the T2b example depend on non-semver internals, which contradicts 'other classes addable later without breaking changes'. Re-exporting future 0.x classes from the 4.x umbrella ties the umbrella's semver to their churn.
issues.fix:
1. Expose accessor functions only: spec(g), params(g), fitinfo(g), selection(g), models(block), and ctx accessors.
2. List every class-author and block-author function as `public` before 1.0, or label the T2 protocol 'experimental: may change in minor releases' in the docs and in the `public` docstrings.
3. Have the umbrella re-export only T0/T1 names. Keep the T2 protocol behind `import StochasticWeatherGeneratorsBlocks as B`.
4. Do not re-export 0.x classes until they reach 1.0.

issues.title: No CI lane tests registered sibling combinations or lower bounds
issues.scenario: Every CI lane develops the siblings by [sources] path. Suppose RegimeHMM 1.1 starts calling a function added in Blocks 1.1 but keeps compat `StochasticWeatherGeneratorsBlocks = "1"`.
issues.what_breaks: Users who resolve Blocks 1.0 (because another package holds it back) get UndefVarError at runtime. CI never sees this because it always uses HEAD of every sibling. The listed Downgrade workflow does not help: path-sourced deps bypass it.
issues.fix:
1. Adopt the OrdinaryDiffEq rule that a sibling's lower bound is bumped whenever new sibling API is used (cf. `OrdinaryDiffEqCore = "4.15.1"`).
2. Add a 'registered siblings' CI lane on release PRs that strips [sources] and resolves the siblings from General at their declared lower bounds.
3. Run Downgrade per lib with siblings taken from the registry.

issues.title: The SPSM coupling is wider than the stated ~12-function contract, and the Downstream job goes silent exactly when it matters
issues.scenario: Blocks uses SPSM `public` internals: norm_cdf_2d_vfast, pairwise_loglikelihood_memory, ar1_sufficient_statistics, PeriodicNLL, update_dist, solve_objective and fit_mle_all_slices. §6.3 marks about 45 names `public`. 5.1 and 5.2 plan a SoftmaxLink dedup, CachedLogDensity and masked emissions. The Downstream job runs only the Blocks and RegimeHMM tests. When SPSM main moves to 5.0.0-DEV, libs with compat "4.2" fail to resolve, and SciML-style downstream templates treat a ResolutionError as a skip.
issues.what_breaks: Under Julia's `public` semantics, any signature change to those kernels is an SPSM major, which forces lockstep majors again; otherwise it silently breaks Blocks. CLG (SmoothDistribution, latent kernels) and WGEN (pairwise kernels) are never tested downstream. During the 5.0 breaking PR the Downstream job reports green without running anything.
issues.fix:
1. Make `public` only the engine contract Blocks actually needs, and list it explicitly. Leave the other internals unmarked, and have Blocks pin those internals with tight compat or vendor them.
2. Have Downstream run all four libs.
3. On SPSM's v5 branch, check out a SWG branch whose compat admits the dev version, and fail on ResolutionError instead of skipping.
4. Add a nightly SWG lane against SPSM main.

issues.title: Numerical changes missing from the intentional-differences list, and an infeasible WGEN Ω tolerance
issues.scenario: Regimes has `order_by = :wetness`. collect_data_INRAE→clean_data deletes leading rows of every variable while an imputed column is missing (src/data/extracting.jl:161-163), whereas WeatherData keeps the complete axis. v3 fit_AR1 calls dropmissing and bridges gaps (ext fit_mle_AR.jl:1, :24-25), affecting the margins as well as cov_ar1. SPSM 5 switches the TVP fit to the average objective; it is unnormalised today (TVP fit.jl:139-149). The WGEN Ω test uses atol 0.03 against v3 fit_Ω, which runs a 2000-day Monte Carlo inside the root find and advances the RNG there (wgen.jl:179). Member seeds are Xoshiro(hash(i, seed)).
issues.what_breaks: Learned or pretrained regimes could be silently relabelled, so `curve(...; regime = 2)`, sims.regime and the my_color ordering no longer match the v3 z_hat or the paper figures. TN, QQ and ETPP fits use extra early days, and AR1 margins change on gappy stations, but neither appears in the intentional-differences list. The v3 Ω estimate itself has a Monte Carlo SD of a few 0.01, so CRN versus v3 differences above 0.03 are routine: with 36+ pair-months the test either fails or gets loosened ad hoc. Ensembles are reproducible only within one Julia and Distributions version, because Base.hash and the samplers are not version-stable.
issues.fix:
1. Never relabel frozen or pretrained regimes, and assert that ẑ labels equal z_hat_K_4_d_1_m_1.csv exactly.
2. Either replicate the leading-row trim in read_stations(INRAE()) or add it to the list. Also add 'AR1 margins drop gap terms' and 'TVP average objective' to the list.
3. Compare WGEN Ω against a high-nsim v3 reference (e.g. 10^6 days) with a tolerance in Monte Carlo SE units, Bonferroni-corrected.
4. Derive member RNGs through a documented seeding (e.g. Xoshiro seeded with [base, i]), and store the Julia and Distributions versions in the WeatherSimulation provenance.

issues.title: CI and docs mechanics for the monorepo are underspecified
issues.scenario: The design proposes a CI.yml with path filters, a Documentation.yml that runs on `tags: '*'` (existing), deploydocs(repo, devbranch = "master") (docs/make.jl:88), a @time_imports gate at 1.5× budget, CompatHelper with subdirs while the repo already uses Dependabot for /, /docs and /test, and lib/X/test projects.
issues.what_breaks: (1) Path-filtered required checks stay 'pending' and block merges, and a Core-only change must still trigger every dependent lib. (2) Each lib tag such as StochasticWeatherGeneratorsCore-v1.0.0 starts a full docs build (37-station tutorial fits) that Documenter then refuses to deploy. 'Stable' docs follow umbrella tags only, so a lib minor's docs are visible only under dev. (3) Import-time gates on shared runners are flaky. (4) Two dependency bots, or neither, end up covering lib/*. (5) lib test envs that are neither listed in a workspace nor declared via [extras]/[targets] will not resolve under Pkg.test.
issues.fix:
1. Use a single always-run workflow with dorny/paths-filter and an explicit dependency map (Core → all).
2. Build docs on `v*` tags only, with tag_prefix set.
3. Track load time as a nightly metric and fail only above 2×.
4. Pick one bot and list every lib directory.
5. Specify per-lib test deps through [extras]/[targets].

issues.title: The umbrella tarball carries about 100 MB of data, and master-relative URLs break at cutover
issues.scenario: The root is the umbrella, so its registered tree includes lib/, weather_files (53 MB) and assets (46 MB). The tutorials download from refs/heads/master paths: tuto_paper.jl:184, :251 and tuto_add_station_variable.jl:139 (assets/tuto_1/hmm_fit_K_4_d_1_m_1.jld). examples/tuto_paper_ascmo.qmd is the paper's reproducibility code.

issues.title: 'Copulas leaves SWG' brings no load-time gain while SPSM still loads it
issues.scenario: SPSM keeps `using Copulas` (SmoothPeriodicStatsModels.jl:15). The only use is the multisite rand at AR/AR1.jl:131-132, which 5.0 moves to Blocks. Copulas 1.0.1 depends on Optim, ForwardDiff, HCubature, Roots and TaylorSeries, among others (SPSM Manifest).

issues.title: The Aqua disambiguation method is type piracy in Blocks
issues.scenario: §7 closes the ambiguity between fit(::Type{<:Distribution}, x) and fit(data, ::AbstractGenerator) with an erroring method defined in Blocks. Blocks owns neither StatsAPI.fit, nor Distribution, nor AbstractGenerator (which belongs to Core).
issues.what_breaks: Aqua's piracy test fails in Blocks. Similar ambiguities exist with StatsBase's fit(::Type{Histogram}, …) and are not caught by testing Core alone.
issues.fix: Define the disambiguations in Core package extensions on Distributions and StatsBase (weakdeps). Run Aqua's ambiguity test on the umbrella with those packages loaded.

confirmations: Subdir registration is standard practice. General's Package.toml for OrdinaryDiffEqCore records repo = OrdinaryDiffEq.jl.git and subdir = "lib/OrdinaryDiffEqCore" (verified in the local General tarball).

The OrdinaryDiffEq root and its sublibraries use [sources] path entries to siblings (root Project.toml; lib/OrdinaryDiffEqTsit5/Project.toml), and the registry ignores [sources]. The design's 'dev only' use of [sources] is sound; only adding [workspace] on top causes the coupling problem.
SPSM 4.0.0 and 4.1.0 are registered in General, so an additive 4.2 and then 5.0 are sequential versions with no AutoMerge skip problem for SPSM.
SPSM and SWG require julia = "1.12", so `public`, [sources] and [workspace] are all available natively. No Compat.@compat is needed.
Leap366's period_index is exactly v3 dayofyear_Leap (SWG src/utilities.jl:15), so Date→t is unchanged.

All 94 SPSM v4 exports (SmoothPeriodicStatsModels.jl:51-199) are assigned in §6.3 to exported, public or removed. fit_loss_optim maps to solve_objective and params/parameters/nparams map to m(t)/coef/dof.
HMM_Spatial_codepaper's Manifest pins SPSM 2.1.2, so 5.0's removals (randARPeriodicHMM, Trig2ARPeriodicHMMSpatial, parameters) do not break it.

The 5.0 change of fit_mle from returning a tuple to returning the model fails loudly: SmoothAR1, the mixture and the HMM types are not iterable, so `m, h = fit_mle(...)` errors instead of mis-destructuring. Making n2t required is also loud.

WGEN counting = :v3 can be bitwise ==. v3 probabilities are integer count/total divisions (wgen.jl:91-101), and p(wet | s) = transition_probs[j][s][[s[2:p]; 1]] (wgen.jl:127) maps one to one onto a closed-form P(O = 1 | h) table.

The L2 noise-injection test against v4 rand(ARs, ϵ, n2t, z, Σ; y₁) is feasible because that method is deterministic given ϵ and never reads Σ (AR1.jl:147-156). GaussianCopula normalises cov_ar1's covariance, so switching to correlation plus nearest_cor does not change the innovations' scale.
Dropping NonlinearSolve and OrderedCollections from SWG is feasible: they are used only by wgen.jl (IntervalNonlinearProblem in fit_Ω, OrderedDict tables), which is being rewritten.
Making the MeteoFrance download lazy correctly removes the network call at precompile time (src/data/extracting.jl:176).
SWG has no test CI today (only Documentation.yml and TagBot.yml, and tests run only as a side effect of the docs build's coverage), so P0 'test CI first' is necessary and can be merged on its own.
Keeping SPSM in its own repo is justified: it has a co-author and its own General history (2.0.3 to 4.1.0), and its domain-agnostic users (tuto_genomics) do not need SWG.
New packages may be registered directly at 1.0.0 under AutoMerge, and the long StochasticWeatherGenerators* names are far enough from existing names to pass the similarity checks.
